ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the circuit diagram is labeled with a 100 V DC input, and the main switch S is connected in series above; the node after the switch is connected to the inductor and 10Ω load on the right, and the node is connected downward to a freewheeling diode D to the lower loop, so this is a buck chopper with a freewheeling diode. Reasoning: The duty cycle of the main switch δ = 0.8, so the average output voltage of the ideal buck chopper is V_o = δ V_s = 0.8 × 100 = 80 V. The load current has no ripple, so the average load current I_o = V_o / R = 80 / 10 = 8 A. Diode D conducts only during the off period of the main switch, and the off duty cycle is 1 - 0.8 = 0.2; when conducting, the diode current is equal to the load current 8 A. Therefore the average diode current I_D(avg) = 0.2 × 8 = 1.6 A.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify a buck chopper with a 10 ohm load and freewheeling diode D. From the text, use V_s = 100 V and duty ratio delta = 0.8. Compute average output voltage V_o = 0.8 * 100 = 80 V. Since the load current is ripple-free, I_o = 80/10 = 8 A. The diode carries this same current during the OFF interval only, which lasts 1 - 0.8 = 0.2 of each cycle. Hence I_D(avg) = 0.2 * 8 = 1.6 A.

method.method_draft: Model the two intervals visible from the chopper circuit. Let the constant load/inductor current be I. During ON time, v_L = 100 - 10I. During OFF time, the diode freewheels the current and the switch node is approximately at the lower rail, so v_L = -10I. Apply inductor volt-second balance: 0.8(100 - 10I) + 0.2(-10I) = 0. This gives 80 - 10I = 0, so I = 8 A. Since D conducts this 8 A only during the OFF fraction 0.2, its average current is 0.2 * 8 = 1.6 A.
